title: Verified numerics (FP64)
hardware: 8x V100 SXM2 box (62 TFLOPS FP64) + EPYC cores running arb/MPFR interval arithmetic
why: Certificate campaigns are interval arithmetic and FP64, not LLM inference. Gaming Ampere is FP64-crippled (0.55 TFLOPS per 3090 — the whole 12-GPU fleet is ~6.6); one used $6k V100 SXM2 server delivers 10x that. CPU core count matters here too.

title: Lean proof search
hardware: 3090 fleet batching 8-32B models via vLLM + EPYC cores running the Lean kernel
why: Millions of candidate tactics per day, each machine-checked by the Lean kernel — hallucination-proof by construction and embarrassingly parallel. Exactly the workload that costs ~$0.50/M tokens locally vs $20-50/M at the frontier. The killer app for a local 24/7 cluster.

title: Route exhaustion & conjecture mining
hardware: 3090 fleet (288 GB) running 400B-class open MoE reasoning models at Q4
why: Wide, cheap, continuous generation and filtering across all routes. Volume matters more than per-token brilliance; survivors get promoted to the rigor layer. Negative results (route-killing) are a product, not a failure.

title: The rigor layer
hardware: Frontier API — Claude Fable 5 for the hardest steps, Opus 5 batch for mid-tier review
why: Proof-direction decisions and §-level audits need the highest available intelligence, but at low volume: hundreds of deep calls a day, not millions. Budget-capped at a few hundred to ~$2k/month. The cluster's findings feed up; only survivors cost frontier tokens.
